label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
deltaNote: Due to expire around Sep 18, 2026 (90 days from the Jun 20 declaration); cocalero federations aligned with Evo Morales have staged an armed vigil ahead of the expiry.

label: Active Blockades
deltaNote: First blockades since all roadblocks cleared Jun 23: an indefinite blockade at Beni's San Pablo bridge and a 48-hour Oruro–Potosí highway ultimatum began Aug 26, 2026 over the diesel-price decree; military and police were preventively deployed near Yapacaní, Santa Cruz, Aug 25.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Aug 27, 2026)
deltaNote: Up from the 15-year peg of Bs. 6.96 before the Jun 29 float; after retreating from a late-July peak near Bs. 12.13 to ~Bs. 11.50 in mid-to-late August, the official rate ticked back up to Bs. 11.71 by Aug 27, with the parallel market at Bs. 11.99

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price — Large Consumers (GRACOS)
deltaNote: Up from the prior Bs. 9.80-9.90/L rate; the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L price is unchanged for transport operators and individual consumers
contestNote: Facing backlash over the 84% hike, Deputy Hydrocarbons Minister Hernán Paredes said Aug 25 the decree "has to be modified" toward a more competitive price. But Minister of the Presidency Fernando Aramayo rejected repeal on Aug 27, attributing the decree to IMF conditionality; new blockades against it began Aug 26 in Beni and Oruro.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
deltaNote: Fernando Cerimedo plus three others (Roger A.C., Paola Andrea V., Fritz Junior G.A.) are now in preventive detention across the Beller shooting and illicit-enrichment cases; prosecutors opened new money-laundering and narco-trafficking-protection probes Aug 27, and President Paz publicly denied any formal contract with Cerimedo the same day.
